sample_unit: patients (All of Us Research Program participants; test set n=696)

links.outcome: Black-White gap in LDL-C estimation error (MAE) for race-free ML model
links.effect: Black-White gap −0.19 mg/dL with CI including zero; ML improvement over Friedewald was 19% for Black patients vs 11% for White patients.
links.quote: The system achieved racial equity without race input (Black-White gap −0.19 mg dL  −1 , CI includes zero) while providing greatest improvement for Black patients (19% vs 11% for White).

unlisted_practices: Using ML to estimate LDL-C accurately from non-fasting samples
Excluding race as a model input to achieve equity
Labs-only configuration for telehealth or home-testing workflows
Economic and break-even analysis of eliminating repeat testing visits

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and validating an ML model for estimating LDL-C in non-fasting and telehealth contexts with a focus on algorithmic equity and economic impact, evaluated retrospectively using the All of Us Research Program dataset.
